key_insight: Separating permanent parametric representations from transient non-parametric representations helps continual reinforcement learning balance knowledge retention and rapid adaptation.
engineering_relevance: This approach could support adaptive engineering agents facing changing conditions, but the abstract provides no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: Decompose value learning into permanent and transient systems.
Use parametric representations for long-term generalization.
Introduce a non-parametric transient value approximation for online adaptation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical and empirical investigation, with performance exceeding competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic.
watch_item: The memory and computational costs of the non-parametric transient representation are not specified in the abstract.
paper_title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
